title: The Core of the Reformed Faith - Living for God’s Glory - 5
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro
series: The Core of the Reformed Faith - Living for God’s Glory

outline.title: Dispelling the Myth of Reformed Passivity
subpoints: Reformed theology does not hinder evangelistic zeal
Historical evidence of Calvinist missionaries (Whitefield, Carey, Spurgeon)
Sovereignty fuels confidence in the gospel's power

outline.title: Calvin’s Theological Foundation for Evangelism
subpoints: Evangelism as a primary object of prayer
The Triune God sends grace to all nations

outline.title: The Responsibility of the Believer
subpoints: Every Christian is an instrument of God’s grace
Proclaiming the full gospel with authority

outline.title: Sovereignty and Human Responsibility
subpoints: The proclamation of the gospel will not fail

summary:
This sermon, the fifth in the series 'Living for God’s Glory,' addresses the common misconception that Reformed theology discourages evangelism. The speaker argues that a true belief in God’s sovereignty actually fuels a passion for missions, citing historical figures like George Whitefield and William Carey as evidence. By examining the teachings of John Calvin, particularly in the *Institutes of the Christian Religion*, the message highlights that evangelism is a central object of prayer and a duty for all believers.

The teaching emphasizes that Christ is actively building His church and that the Triune God sends His grace to all corners of the earth. Therefore, believers are called to be faithful instruments of this grace, proclaiming the full gospel with confidence. The sermon distinguishes between modern 'sharing' and biblical 'proclaiming,' urging the congregation to rely on the power of the Word rather than human effort.

Ultimately, the message reconciles divine sovereignty with human responsibility. While salvation is God’s work, Christians are commanded to preach the gospel everywhere. The assurance that the proclamation of the gospel will not fail provides the motivation for believers to engage in evangelism, trusting that God will gather His church from all nations.
